items.title: Section: Attainment Itself — Neither Form Nor Mind, Yet Established Upon Both

items.zh: 問：諸蘊分位有幾種？答：有多種。謂得、無想定等心不相應行，廣說如前。問：依何分位建立得？此復幾種？答：依因、自在、現行分位建立得。此復三種，謂種子成就、自在成就、現行成就。
items.en: Question: how many kinds of stage do the aggregates have? Answer: many — attainment, the two mindless meditative states, and the rest, as already extensively explained. Question: upon what basis is attainment established, and how many kinds are there? Answer: it is established upon the basis of cause, mastery, and manifestation. It is further of three kinds: attainment through seed, attainment through mastery, and attainment through manifestation.

items.zh: 問：依何分位建立無想定、滅盡定及無想天？此三各有幾種？

items.title: Section: The Mindless Attainment — Ordinary Beings Mistaking Silence for Liberation

items.zh: 答：依已離遍淨貪，未離上貪，出離想作意為先名滅分位，建立無想定。此復三種。自性者，唯是善。補特伽羅者，在異生相續。起者，先於此起，後於色界第四靜慮當受彼果。
items.en: Answer: it is established upon the stage of cessation preceded by attention to the perception of escape, arising once craving for Universal Purity, the third absorption's highest heaven, has already been overcome, though craving for what lies above it has not. This is further of three kinds. Its own nature is invariably wholesome. Those who cultivate it belong to the continuity of ordinary, unenlightened beings. As for how it arises: it first arises here, in the desire realm, and its result is subsequently experienced in the form realm's fourth absorption.

items.title: Section: Cessation Attainment — Reserved for the Noble, and a Debate Over Whether It Needs a Body at All

items.zh: 依已離無所有處貪，止息想作意為先名滅分位，建立滅盡定。此復三種。自性者，唯是善。補特伽羅者，在聖相續，通學無學。起者，先於此起，後於色界重現在前，託色所依方現前故。此據未建立阿賴耶識教。若已建立，於一切處皆得現前。
items.en: It is established upon the stage of cessation preceded by attention to the perception of stilling, arising once craving for the sphere of nothingness has already been overcome. This is further of three kinds. Its own nature is invariably wholesome. Those who cultivate it belong to the continuity of noble ones, spanning both learners and those beyond learning. As for how it arises: according to teachings not yet establishing the storehouse consciousness, it must first arise here and then manifest again in the form realm, requiring a physical basis to actually appear. Once this doctrine is established, it may manifest anywhere at all.

items.title: Section: The Mindless Heaven Itself — A Rebirth Destination, Purely Neutral, Reserved for the Mistaken

items.zh: 依已生無想有情天中名滅分位，建立無想。此亦三種。自性者，無覆無記。補特伽羅者，唯異生性，彼非諸聖者。起者，謂能引發無想定思，能感彼異熟果；後想生已，是諸有情便從彼沒。
items.en: It is established upon the stage of cessation already reached by beings born into the mindless heaven. This is likewise of three kinds. Its own nature is unobscured and neutral. Those born there belong exclusively to the continuity of ordinary beings, never noble ones. As for how it unfolds: the volition capable of generating this attainment brings about its karmic result upon rebirth; once perception arises again, such beings pass away from that state.

items.zh: 問：依何分位建立命根？此復幾種？

items.title: Section: The Life Faculty — Fixed or Uncertain, Welcome or Unwelcome, Counted in Years or in Eons

items.zh: 答：依業所引異熟住時決定分位，建立命根。此復三種。謂定不定故，愛非愛故，歲劫數等所安立故。
items.en: Answer: the life faculty is established upon the settled duration karma has determined a given karmic result will last. It is further of three kinds: fixed or uncertain, desirable or undesirable, and measured in years, eons, and so on.

items.zh: 問：依何分位建立眾同分？此復幾種？

items.title: Section: Species-Similarity, and Three Faces of Arising — Instant by Instant, Life to Life, Mood to Mood

items.zh: 答：依諸有情相似分位，立眾同分。此復三種。所謂種類同分、自性同分、工巧業處養命同分。問：依何分位建立生？此復幾種？答：依現在分位，建立生。此復三種。所謂剎那生、相續生、分位生。
items.en: Answer: species-similarity is established upon the shared resemblance among various beings. It is of three kinds: similarity of category, similarity of essential character, and similarity through shared trade or livelihood. Answer: arising is established upon the present moment. It is of three kinds: momentary arising, continuous arising, and arising through distinct stages.

items.zh: 問：依何分位建立老？此復幾種？

items.title: Section: Ageing in Three Faces — And Why the Body May Suffer While the Mind Need Not

items.zh: 答：依前後分位，建立老。此復三種。謂異性老、轉變老、受用老。
items.en: Answer: ageing is established upon the difference between an earlier and a later stage. It is of three kinds: ageing through changed character, ageing through transformation, and ageing in enjoyment.

items.zh: 問：依何分位建立住？此復幾種？

items.title: Section: Abiding and Impermanence — Momentary Persistence, and Three Ways Everything Eventually Falls Apart

items.zh: 答：即依生分位，建立住。此復三種。謂剎那住、相續住、立制住。問：依何分位建立無常？此復幾種？答：依生已壞滅分位，建立無常。此復三種。謂壞滅無常、轉變無常、別離無常。
items.en: Answer: abiding is established upon the very stage of arising. It is of three kinds: momentary abiding, continuous abiding, and abiding through established convention. Answer: impermanence is established upon the stage in which what has arisen subsequently breaks apart. It is of three kinds: impermanence through destruction, impermanence through transformation, and impermanence through separation.

items.zh: 問：依何分位建立名身？此復幾種？

items.title: Section: Names, Phrases, and Syllables — And Why a Raised Eyebrow Can Teach the Dharma Too

items.zh: 答：依假言說分位，建立名身。此復三種。謂假設名身、實物名身、世所共了不了名身。如名身，句身、文身，當知亦爾。此中差別者，謂標句、釋句、音所攝、字所攝。
items.en: Answer: a name-group is established upon provisional linguistic convention. It is of three kinds: provisional names, substantive names, and names either commonly understood or not commonly understood. As with names, so too with phrases and syllables. The distinction here is between declarative and explanatory phrases, and between what is subsumed under sound and what is subsumed under letters.

items.zh: 問：依何分位建立異生性？此復幾種？

items.title: Section: Ordinary-Being Status Across Three Realms, and Continuity's Forward and Reverse Flow

items.zh: 答：依未生起一切出世聖法分位，建立異生性。此復三種。謂欲界繫、色界繫、無色界繫。問：依何分位建立流轉？此復幾種？答：依因果相續分位，建立流轉。此復三種。謂剎那展轉流轉、生展轉流轉、染污清淨展轉流轉。
items.en: Answer: ordinary-being status is established upon the stage in which every supramundane, noble quality remains unrealized. It is of three kinds: bound to the desire realm, the form realm, and the formless realm. Answer: continuity is established upon the uninterrupted succession of cause and effect. It is of three kinds: momentary continuity, continuity through rebirth, and continuity through defilement and purification.

items.zh: 問：依何分位建立定異？此復幾種？

items.title: Section: Cause Never Blurs With Effect — Determinate Distinction and the Beginning of Correspondence

items.zh: 答：依法別相分位，建立定異。此復三種。謂相定異、因定異、果定異。問：依何分位建立相應？此復幾種？
items.en: Answer: determinate distinction is established upon each phenomenon's own distinct, non-blurring characteristic. It is of three kinds: distinction of characteristic, distinction of cause, and distinction of effect. Question: upon what basis is correspondence established, and how many kinds are there?

items.title: Section: Correspondence's Three Faces, and Three Speeds — From a Single Thought to a Buddha's Own Reach

items.zh: 答：依因果相稱分位，建立相應。此復三種。謂和合相應、方便相應、稱可道理所作相應。問：依何分位建立勢速？此復幾種？答：依迅疾流轉分位，建立勢速。此復三種。謂諸行勢速、士用勢速、神通勢速。
items.en: Answer: correspondence is established upon the fitting match between cause and effect. It is of three kinds: correspondence through combination, through skilful means, and through conformity with principle. Answer: speed is established upon the swift, unceasing flow of form and mind. It is of three kinds: the speed of conditioned phenomena, of embodied beings, and of supernatural power.

items.zh: 問：依何分位建立次第？此復幾種？

blocks.text: Fascicle 56 runs through the "formations dissociated from mind" once more, briefly: each is a name set upon some phase of form or mind (Days 464–468).
Set upon cause, mastery, and manifestation. Master Cháng Bǎi: attainment is provisionally set upon mind, mental factors, and form.
Set upon the stage in which the first six consciousnesses cease. Master Cháng Bǎi: those who cultivate it wrongly take the heaven of no-perception for nirvāṇa.

The need for a physical basis holds only in teachings that have not yet established the store-consciousness. Master Cháng Bǎi: even formless beings, without a body, are held together by the store-consciousness.
The attainment is wholesome; the state of no-perception in that heaven is neutral.
Set upon the fixed duration of a ripened result drawn by karma. Master Cháng Bǎi: the span of one life, decided by past karma.
Master Cháng Bǎi: beings of one realm or destiny resemble one another.
Master Cháng Bǎi: if the mind does not cling to the five aggregates as self, the mind does not age; the body may suffer while the mind does not.
Momentary, continuous, and conventional abiding. Master Cháng Bǎi: laws set for a people are "conventional abiding".
Master Cháng Bǎi: where what a name refers to has no real substance, it is a provisional name.
Ordinary-being status rests on not yet realising the suchness of the two emptinesses. Master Cháng Bǎi: as the prior cause ceases the result arises, like the two ends of a scale.
Master Cháng Bǎi: good and evil causes are fixed in their difference; good causes bring human and heavenly results.
"If the mind does not cling to the aggregates as self, the mind does not age." Master Cháng Bǎi's line is worth carrying into later life.

quiz.q: Upon what basis is attainment established, and what are its three kinds?
options: upon cause, mastery, and manifestation; attainment through seed, through mastery, and through manifestation
upon past, present, and future; attained, attaining, and to be attained, since attainment must span the three times
upon discipline, concentration, and wisdom; attainment of learners, adepts, and ordinary beings
upon form, mind, and mental factors; attainment of each
quiz.why: The treatise establishes attainment upon cause, mastery, and manifestation, and names three kinds. Master Cháng Bǎi: attainment is provisionally set upon mind, mental factors, and form; a seed not yet suppressed or severed has the potential to yield its result, and is the distant cause of its manifestation, and this is called attainment.

quiz.q: Upon what stage is the attainment of no-thought set, and why do only ordinary beings cultivate it, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: the ceasing of the first six consciousnesses' mind and factors; ordinary beings mistake the heaven of no-thought for nirvāṇa
the ceasing of the eighth consciousness; noble ones also cultivate it but do not speak of it, so it only seems confined to ordinary beings
the ceasing of the body; ordinary beings cultivate it from fear of death
the ceasing of seeds; ordinary beings who have severed afflictions cultivate it
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the attainment of no-thought is established upon the stage in which mind and factors of the first six consciousnesses cease. Those who cultivate it wrongly take the heaven of no-thought to be nirvāṇa, regarding what is not cessation as cessation. So though the attainment itself is wholesome, the view behind it keeps noble ones from it.

quiz.q: How does establishing the store-consciousness change where the attainment of cessation can arise?
options: under teachings without it, it manifests anywhere; once established, only in the form realm, since that consciousness needs a body
no difference: both only in the desire realm
no difference: both only in the formless realm
under teachings without it, it needs a physical basis; once established, it may manifest anywhere
quiz.why: The treatise says the need for a physical basis holds under teachings not yet establishing the store-consciousness. Master Cháng Bǎi: though formless beings have no body, the store-consciousness is present, so even in cessation there is no danger of total annihilation; entering it is not death but a temporary rest of mind and factors.

quiz.q: What is the nature of the attainment of no-thought and of the no-thought heaven, and why do they differ?
options: the attainment is unobscured-neutral; the heaven is wholesome, heavenly birth being a good result
both are unwholesome, being outsiders' practice, which is why noble ones avoid them and both lead to a fall
the attainment is invariably wholesome; the heaven is unobscured-neutral, spoken of by way of the store-consciousness
both are obscured-neutral
quiz.why: The treatise says the attainment is invariably wholesome, and the state of no-thought in that heaven is unobscured and neutral. Master Cháng Bǎi: absorption is a wholesome phenomenon, whereas birth in the heaven is explained through the store-consciousness and is unobscured-neutral. The practice and its ripened result thus differ in moral quality.

quiz.q: Upon what is the life faculty established?
options: the continuing stage of breathing, the life faculty ending when breath stops, unrelated to karma
the stage of being sustained by food
the settled duration that karma has determined a ripened result will last
the stage of parents' union
quiz.why: The treatise establishes the life faculty upon the settled duration of a ripened result drawn by karma. Master Cháng Bǎi: the life faculty is the span of one life, decided by past karma; "fixed" means a set lifespan, as the people of Uttarakuru live a thousand years with no premature death.

quiz.q: What are the three kinds of species-similarity?
options: similarity of category, of essential character, and of trade or livelihood
of past, present, and future, set by the three times, making similarity a phase of time
of precepts, views, and gain
of the three realms
quiz.why: The treatise names three. Master Cháng Bǎi: beings of one realm or destiny resemble one another, which is similarity of category; essential-character similarity subdivides this further; and sameness of occupation or skill is the third. The English "species-similarity" serves here, though the previous fascicle's renderings differ.

quiz.q: The English has "ageing through diminished capacity" for 受用老, while §19 has "fully experienced" for 受用. How does this compare with the lecture?
options: the lecture: 受用 is enjoying wealth, so this is loss of wealth, and the English should say that
the lecture: it means having held precepts for long
the lecture: it means the mind not ageing
the lecture: the faculties' enjoyment of objects declines; "diminished capacity" is an interpretive addition, and 受用 has two renderings
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: differing nature of form and mind from before to after is ageing through changed character; the decline of the faculties' enjoyment of objects is 受用老. So the sense is declining enjoyment. "Diminished capacity" gets at this, but it drops the word, and §19 renders 受用 as "fully experienced," so a reader cannot connect them.

quiz.q: Ageing is set upon earlier and later stages. How, per Master Cháng Bǎi, may the mind not age, and what of the body?
options: by practices of long life neither body nor mind ages, so noble ones' bodies do not age, only ordinary beings' do
the body does not age while the mind does, afflictions increasing
if the mind does not cling to the aggregates as self, it does not age; the body still has ageing and death through past karma
neither ages, ageing being a mere name, with nothing really changing
quiz.why: The treatise establishes ageing upon earlier and later stages. Master Cháng Bǎi: if the mind does not cling to the five aggregates as self, the mind does not age; though the mind is free of suffering, the body still suffers, past karma bringing ageing, sickness, and death to it. This reflects the earlier teaching of body-feeling without mind-feeling.

quiz.q: What are the three kinds of abiding and of impermanence?
options: abiding: destruction, transformation, separation; impermanence: momentary, continuous, by convention, since conventions change
abiding: the three realms; impermanence: the three moral qualities
abiding: walking, standing, sitting; impermanence: birth, ageing, death
abiding: momentary, continuous, by convention; impermanence: destruction, transformation, separation
quiz.why: The treatise names momentary, continuous, and conventional abiding, and impermanence through destruction, transformation, and separation. Master Cháng Bǎi: laws and regulations set for a people or a family are abiding by established convention; desirable phenomena turning undesirable is impermanence through transformation.

quiz.q: What are the three kinds of name-group, and upon what is it established?
options: upon really existing phenomena: names of form, mind, and factors, names belonging to phenomena by nature
upon the Buddha's speech: names of sūtra, vinaya, and treatise
upon the three times: past, future, and present names
upon provisional convention: provisional names, substantive names, and names commonly understood or not
quiz.why: The treatise sets name-groups upon provisional convention and gives three kinds. Master Cháng Bǎi: where what a name depends on has no real substance, it is a provisional name; names, phrases, and syllables are all provisionally set upon form, sound, and mental objects, with no substance of their own.

quiz.q: Upon what is the status of an ordinary being established?
options: upon the stage in which every supramundane, noble quality remains unrealized
upon the stage in which all afflictions have arisen, only those with manifest afflictions counting as ordinary beings
upon the stage of not having taken precepts
upon the stage of birth in the desire realm
quiz.why: The treatise sets ordinary-being status upon the stage in which supramundane noble qualities remain unrealized. Master Cháng Bǎi: it rests on not yet having realised the suchness of the two emptinesses; it refers to the seeds to be severed by seeing in the three realms, by which beings have different views, make different karma, and receive different results.

quiz.q: Continuity rests on cause and effect. How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain momentary and defilement-and-purification continuity?
options: the prior cause never ceases, results piling up; pure and defiled minds cannot succeed each other, one excluding the other forever
cause and result coexist with no before or after
the prior cause ceases and the result arises, like the two ends of a scale; ordinary beings' pure and defiled minds of three qualities continue unbroken
continuity means rebirth only, unrelated to moments
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: as the prior cause ceases the result arises, like the two ends of a scale, one rising as the other falls at the same time; and ordinary beings sometimes have a defiled mind, sometimes a pure one, the minds of three moral qualities continuing unbroken. The English "continuity" for 流轉 here differs from "transformation" in fascicle 52.

quiz.q: What are the three determinate distinctions, and how are those of cause and effect explained?
options: of characteristic, cause, and effect; good causes bring human and heavenly joy, evil causes the evil destinies, and results are fixed in their difference
of seed, manifestation, and infusion; good causes at times bring pain and evil ones joy, so cause and effect are not fixed but vary with conditions
of form, mind, and dissociated phenomena
of upper, middle, and lower
quiz.why: The treatise establishes determinate distinction upon each phenomenon's own distinct characteristic. Master Cháng Bǎi: good and evil causes are fixed in their difference, good causes bringing human and heavenly joy and evil causes the suffering of the evil destinies; and painful and pleasant results are fixed, each joined with its feeling. Each has cause and result distinct, not blurred.

quiz.q: What examples does Master Cháng Bǎi give for the three kinds of correspondence?
options: mind with factors; eye with form; form with smell, all three being relations of simultaneous arising
five precepts and ten good deeds bring heavenly joy; recitation, bowing, and the mindfulnesses are means; wisdom matching truth
teacher and disciple; husband and wife; ruler and minister
earth with water; fire with wind; space with consciousness
quiz.why: The treatise sets correspondence upon the fit between cause and effect. Master Cháng Bǎi gives good causes bringing pleasant results, as the five precepts and ten good deeds bring human and heavenly joy; recitation, bowing, and the mindfulnesses before accomplishment as means; and wisdom matching truth. This is not the association of mind and factors in §28.
